primary_metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations by source package (pinned snapshot)
uncertainty: Three verified C SQL paths. Search: a bounded Debian popcon source-name search (names containing 'sql', first 100 of 229 by rank) plus targeted lookups in the same pinned popcon snapshot, captured 2026-11-17; further targeted lookups in that snapshot on 2026-11-18 (source packages outside the first 100 'sql' hits, tree-sitter grammar sources); vcpkg and Conan Center; the GitHub search 'sql parser language:C' (discovery only); and, under the C and C++ GitHub-star fallback (2026-11-18: tagged upstream release, at least 100 stars, format-specific parser repository; ranked after popcon paths), twenty bounded GitHub repository searches with stars:>=100 (first 100 results each, recorded in the registry snapshot). Selected: libgda 5.2.10 (Debian source libgda5, 2,105 installations) parses both valid controls with its generic Lemon-generated GdaSqlParser into a GdaSqlStatement tree, and libpg_query 18.1.0 (Debian source libpg-query, 41) parses them with the PostgreSQL 18 grammar; both trees give the oracle summary. tree-sitter-sql 0.3.11 (Debian source tree-sitter-sql, 8 installations, rank 3 of 3) is the DerekStride grammar (generated parser.c and scanner.c, byte-identical to Debian 0.3.11-1) on the tree-sitter 0.26.11 C runtime; it builds a concrete syntax tree that gives the oracle summary for both controls, and because tree-sitter is error-tolerant the adapter rejects trees with ERROR or MISSING nodes. Metric caveats: the libgda and libpg_query popcon counts are small or library-wide (libgda's covers the whole data-access library) and reflect packaged installs, not use of SQL parsing. tree-sitter-sql's count is the weakest in the cell and measures the only binary package of that source, the Python binding python3-tree-sitter-sql, not C use. Exclusions: sqlite3, sqlcipher and postgresql-18 rank higher but are engines or a server without a library syntax-tree API. Further snapshot sources (mariadb, unixodbc, spatialite, freetds, psqlodbc, mdbtools; C++ candidates are in the C++ cell) are a server and client, a driver manager, drivers, a SQLite extension, or a grammar without JOIN, GROUP BY or INSERT (libmdbsql). The other snapshot lookups (tree-sitter runtime, virtuoso-opensource, cowsql, dqlite, mydumper, sqliteodbc, pgpool2, tarantool, libcypher-parser) are a grammar-less runtime, engines, middleware with an internal PostgreSQL parser copy, a backup tool, a driver or a Cypher parser. vcpkg and Conan Center list no C SQL parser besides libpg-query. The GitHub search found sqliteai/liteparser, a C SQLite-grammar AST library with no Debian, vcpkg or Conan package and therefore no admissible metric (recorded as unresolved_no_primary_metric; 35 stars, below the star threshold). No other C source package in the snapshot was found with a documented SQL syntax-tree API, and no unranked C path exists for the Debian development-package fallback. The star-fallback searches found no new C path: libpg_query (1,494 stars) and tree-sitter-sql (250) are already selected by popcon; sqlite-createtable-parser (138) parses only CREATE TABLE; libinjection (1,031) is an injection tokenizer; pg_query_go and pg_query are Go and Ruby bindings; the rest are engines, extensions and tools. Evidence for every exclusion is in leads.json. The cell stops at three paths, not ten. Two valid controls establish only the tested dialect-neutral subset.
